records: The Connected Nations Planned Network Deployments 2026 report was published on 13 May 2026.
The report examines anticipated full-fibre network coverage through the end of 2028.
The report examines anticipated gigabit-capable network coverage through the end of 2028.
The report covers fixed-wireless-access network extension and upgrade plans for very-high-speed broadband.
The report is based on network operators' stated deployment plans as of January 2026.
The stated deployment plans cover the following three years.
The deployment plans include both privately funded and publicly supported plans.
The report does not separately count rollout aspirations of national or local public authorities.
The forward-looking report supplements the Connected Nations Spring 2026 coverage snapshot.
Ofcom estimated that full fibre could reach 28.1 million UK homes by January 2029 if all stated plans are realised.
Ofcom estimated that full fibre could reach 92% of UK residential properties by January 2029 if all stated plans are realised.
The January 2026 full-fibre baseline was 24.9 million homes, or 82%.
Ofcom estimated that gigabit-capable coverage could reach 29 million homes by January 2029.
Ofcom estimated that gigabit-capable coverage could reach 95% by January 2029.
The January 2026 gigabit-capable baseline was 27.1 million homes, or 89%.
High-confidence full-fibre plans could produce 87% coverage by January 2028.
High-confidence full-fibre plans could produce 88% coverage by January 2029.
If all plans are realised, rural gigabit-capable coverage could rise from 2.9 million homes (66%) to 3.7 million homes (86%) by January 2029.
Ofcom estimated that 22.2 million homes, or 73%, could have access to at least two gigabit-capable networks by the end of 2028.
Around 6,950 additional geographically distinct FWA masts were planned or set for upgrade between January 2026 and January 2029.
Ofcom published the one-million-user Map Your Mobile update on 29 May 2026.
Ofcom reported that one million people had used Map Your Mobile.
Map Your Mobile is a free Ofcom mobile coverage checker.
Users can enter a postcode to compare mobile networks in a particular area.
The checker shows a performance score for companies at postal-district level.
Ofcom presents the checker as a tool for researching networks before signing up or switching.
The checker combines Opensignal crowdsourced experience data with predictive information from UK mobile networks.
Ofcom states that the checker is regularly updated with fresh data.
The checker can indicate whether coverage is likely to work inside a home.
Map Your Mobile users can share feedback through the service.
